title: Strange Printer
statement:
A typist has a blank strip of paper with room for `n` characters and has to produce a given string `s` of letters. In a single turn the typist chooses a contiguous range of positions and a letter, and types that letter into **every** position of the range, overwriting whatever was there before.

Return the **minimum number of turns** needed to turn the blank strip into exactly `s`.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of turns.

examples.explanation: Type `a` over all six positions, then type `b` over positions 3 to 4.
Type `a` over the whole strip, then `b` over positions 2 to 4, then `c` at position 3. Fewer than 3 turns cannot work because three different letters appear.
Type `a` over positions 1 to 3, then `b` over positions 2 to 4, then `a` at position 3.

hints: Think of the turns as nested or disjoint intervals: a later turn can overwrite part of an earlier one, but crossing intervals can always be rearranged into nested ones.

Let f(i, j) be the minimum turns for the substring s[i..j]. Consider the first character: either type it alone for one turn and solve s[i+1..j], or it shares a turn with some later position k where s[k] == s[i].
If s[i] and s[k] are typed in the same turn, that turn can be extended for free: f(i, j) = min over such k of f(i+1, k-1) + f(k, j). Fill the table by increasing substring length.
